name: Cetirizine topical

lead: Cetirizine is a common oral allergy drug. A topical version was tested in 66 women with androgenetic alopecia.
Results were not available to this entry.

paras: Blocks H1 receptors; the hair rationale involves PGD2-related inflammation.
Oral cetirizine can cause drowsiness; topical scalp safety was not reviewed.

trials.title: Topical Cetirizine in Androgenetic Alopecia in Females

lead: Topical cetirizine is a lotion form of the second-generation antihistamine cetirizine, tested for androgenetic alopecia based on the idea that prostaglandin D2 (PGD2) contributes to hair-follicle miniaturisation.[1]
A phase 2/3 trial, NCT04481412, in 66 women with androgenetic alopecia was completed after starting in 2020; no results were loaded for this article.[2]

paras: Cetirizine selectively blocks peripheral histamine H1 receptors and has described anti-inflammatory effects involving NF-kB suppression.[1]

Oral use commonly causes drowsiness, dry mouth and headache; after prolonged daily use, stopping can cause severe itching, per an FDA Drug Safety Communication in May 2025.[1] Topical scalp safety data were not reviewed.
A registered phase 2/3 trial (NCT04481412) of topical cetirizine in 66 women with androgenetic alopecia was completed; results were not available in the sources used.[2]

timeline.event: Female androgenetic alopecia trial of topical cetirizine begins.[2]
